To be honest, this scene is practically tailor-made for those who deal with the devil.

On Wednesday's episode of "The Daily Show," host Josh Johnson pointed out a detail from Donald Trump Jr.'s wedding that looked like it was cut straight from a hit horror film—and once you've seen it, you can't "unsee" it.

Johnson first played footage from the wedding that Trump Jr. had shared on social media. His wife is socialite Bettina Trump, and the wedding took place in May on a small island in the Bahamas.

The clip was set to an acoustic version of The Ronettes' classic "Be My Baby." It began with an overhead shot of the church where the president's eldest son was holding his ceremony, then showed the interior with guests. Trump Jr.'s two sisters, Ivanka and Tiffany Trump, could be seen seated on a bench, followed by a slow-motion shot of the bride and groom embracing at the altar beneath a massive cross.

"Just like that church in 'Sinners,' the wedding was really beautiful," Johnson said with a laugh, with a still from the Oscar-winning film shown beside him—featuring Sammie (played by Miles Caton) walking into his father's church covered in blood. Above Sammie—just as above Trump Jr. and his bride—hung a massive cross. The exterior of the church in 'Sinners' also bears a striking resemblance to the one in the Bahamas.

Trump Jr.'s wedding drew widespread attention because ProPublica had earlier reported that the cost of the wedding was paid for by Russian oligarch Umar Kremlev, who has close ties to Russian President Vladimir Putin.

In response to the controversy, Bettina Trump posted a statement on Instagram clarifying: "Don and I got married privately on Friday with only our families around us."

She continued: "The weekend that followed had been planned well in advance as a fun weekend with friends. It was never intended to be our wedding weekend. Our original wedding plans changed, so we simply got married earlier and then attended the already-planned weekend event as a newlywed couple."

She also wrote that the couple's "good friend Umar was incredibly generous and hosted two wonderful nights of celebrations for us after our wedding."

Johnson had a rather funny response to Bettina Trump's clarification.

"Oh yes, of course, it's fake news," Johnson said, mimicking Bettina Trump's tone. "They didn't pay for my wedding—they paid for the much more expensive after-party."

The full segment also featured plenty of hilarious pop-ups about Tiffany Trump, so you can watch the whole clip above.
